question.problem:
Evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}4xy\,dV
$$

where the region $R$ is given by

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,x\le y\le \sqrt{1-z}\},
$$

and $D$ is a finite region in $xz$-plane enclosed between the $x$-axis, the $z$-axis, and the curve $z=1-{x}^{2},$ in the first quadrant.
question.worked_solution:
Writing down our triple integral as a mixed integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}4xy\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{x}^{\sqrt{1-z}}4xy\,dy]dA.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y,$ treating $x$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{x}^{\sqrt{1-z}}4xy\,dy]dA & ={∬}_{D}2x[{y}^{2}]_{y=x}^{y=\sqrt{1-z}}\,dA \\  & ={∬}_{D}2x(\,(1-z)-{x}^{2})\,dA \\  & ={∬}_{D}2x(1-z)-2{x}^{3}\,dA\end{aligned}
$$

We must now evaluate this double integral over the region $D$ in the $xz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217845/assets/95a2b4e28dbfae5ce447b3b975b2f74bf04883441217f42a24636970948402a0.png)

  

We can evaluate our double integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}2x(1-z)-2{x}^{3}\,dA & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-z}}2x(1-z)-2{x}^{3}\,dx\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(1-z)[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-z}}2x\,dx]dz+{\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-z}}-2{x}^{3}\,dx]dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(1-z)[{x}^{2}]_{x=0}^{x=\sqrt{1-z}}dz+{\int }_{0}^{1}{[-\frac{{x}^{4}}{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=\sqrt{1-z}}dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(1-z)^{2}\,dz-\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}(1-z)^{2}\,dz \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}(1-z)^{2}\,dz \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{[-(1-z)^{3}]}_{z=0}^{z=1} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\end{aligned}
$$
